stem: The British Government decided and declared to leave India by June, 1948 in :
expl: Prime Minister of Britain Attlee declared in the House of Commons on February, 20, 1947 AD that British will leave India before June, 1948 AD, after transferring power to liable people. Attlee appointed Lord Mountbatten as the Viceroy of India in place of Wavell. Mountbatten initiated the efforts of power transfer in March, 1947 AD.

stem: Lord Mountbatten came to India as a Viceroy along with specifi c instruction to –

options.label: d
options.text: Persuade the Congress to accept partition

expl: The Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Clement Attlee announced on 20th February, 1947 AD in the House of Commons that he wish to transfer powers to India but also said that if in time the decision related to the constitution is not made British Empire has the power to transfer Government to any of them. Thus, to effect the transfer of power, Attlee decided to send Lord Mountbatten as Viceroy to India. Lord Mountbatten armed with vast powers became India’s Viceroy on 24 March, 1947 AD. Mountbatten became Viceroy of India with a mandate to oversee the British withdrawal. Lord Mountbatten came to India as Viceroy of India along with specifi c instructions to keep India United if possible however he was authorized to make decisions according to favourable Indian circumstances and minimum British loss. Mountbatten concluded that a United India was an unachievable goal and resigned himself to a plan for partition, creating the independent nations of India and Pakistan.

stem: Which plan became the platform of Indian Independence?
expl: Lord Mountbatten came to India in March, 1947 AD with the purpose to give complete independence to India. He decided 15 August, 1947 AD as the date for power transfer. He made a plan of partition of India under instructions of Attlee which was considered as Mountbatten Plan.

stem: Which Act provided for the partition of India into two new dominions - India and Pakistan?
expl: The Indian Independence Act, 1947, passed by the British Parliament, formally approved the partition of British India and provided the legal basis for the creation of two new independent dominions–India and Pakistan.

stem: The British Parliament passed the Indian Independence Act in –

stem: The Indian Independence Bill received the Royal Assent on –
expl: The Indian Independence Act of 1947 was an implementation of the Mountbatten Plan. The Indian Independence Act was presented in the House of commons of British Parliament on July 4, 1947 AD by the then Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, Clement Attlee. The Indian Independence Act was passed by the House of Commons on July 15, 1947 AD and next day by the House of Lords. Finally, it received royal assent on July 18, 1947 AD.

stem: The Balkan Plan for fragmentation of India was the brain child of –
expl: After arriving in India to negotiate terms for an Independent India, Mountbatten soon concluded that transfer of power to one central representative constituency assembly for India would be impossible to achieve as neither the India National Congress nor the Muslim League could agree to the terms, and he accordingly came up with ‘Plan Balkan’, separate dominion for Pakistan, the Princely States and the rest of British India with certain key areas of administration run by Central Government.

stem: The Indian National Congress agreed in 1947 to the partition of the country mainly because –

options.label: a

options.label: b
options.text: It was imposed by the British Government and the Congress was helpless in this regard.

options.label: c
options.text: They wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots.

options.label: d
options.text: India would have otherwise lost the opportunity to attain freedom.

expl: Attlee announced the appointment of Lord Mountbatten as Viceroy replacing Lord Wavell. Lord Mountbatten, the last British Governor-General and Viceroy arrived in India in March, 1947 AD and immediately began to take measures for the transfer of power. The prevailing communal violence in the country led Mountbatten to announce the partition plan on 3rd June, 1947 AD. The Congress leaders too had come to the conclusion that partition was the only choice to check the widespread communal violence and bloodshed that was ravaging the country. The plan provided for the immediate transfer of power on the basis of the grant of Dominion Status. The Indian National Congress agreed to the partition of the Country mainly because they wanted to avoid large-scale communal riots.

stem: As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that he –

options.label: b
options.text: Invite Jinnah to form the Government.

options.label: c
options.text: Invite Nehru and Jinnah to form the Government together.

options.label: d
options.text: Invite the army to take over for some time.

expl: The fi rst meeting between Gandhiji and Mountbatten took place on 31st March, 1947 AD. As an alternative to the partition of India, Gandhiji suggested to Mountbatten that the best course would be to ask Jinnah to take over as Prime Minister of Interim Government and run the affairs of the Country but this suggestion of Gandhiji was not acceptable to Congress Leaders and Congress Working Committee. He told his attendants: “Today I fi nd myself all alone. Even Sardar and Jawaharlal think that he was wrong, and peace was sure to return if the partition was agreed upon. Nevertheless, I must speak as I feel ... we may not feel the full impact immediately, but, I can see clearly that the future of independence gained at this price is going to be dark. Should the evil I apprehend overtake India ... let posterity know what agony this old soul went through, thinking of it.... Let it not be said that Gandhi was party to Indian vivisection.”

expl: Viceroy of British India, Lord Mountbatten formed two commissions namely Punjab Border Commission and Bengal Border Commission to decide the borderline between India and Pakistan on June 30, 1947 AD. Cyril Radcliffe was appointed as President of both the Commissions. Those Commissions had to demarcate borders by Muslims and Non-Muslims population. They had to consider other factors too. There were four members (judges) in each Commission of which two were from Indian National Congress and two from the Muslim League.

expl: Bengal and Punjab boundary commissions were established in 1947 AD under chairmanship of British lawyer Cyril Radcliffe for the purpose of determining new border between India and Pakistan following independence from British rule. stem: The last opportunity to avoid the partition of India was lost with the rejection of:
expl: The Cabinet Mission of India of 1946 AD had come up with a plan on 16 May, 1946 AD which intended to create a United India with independent Muslim and Hindu majority provinces in which demand of Pakistan raised by Muslim League was rejected, but Muslim League approved the plan on 6th June,1946 AD. On July 29, it rejected the plan and called the Muslims to resort to “Direct Action” to achieve the land of their dream “Pakistan.” August 16, 1946 AD was fi xed as “Direct Action Day.“ As a result , the last opportunity to avoid the partition of India was lost with the rejection of Cabinet Mission.

stem: Which of the following assumed sovereign power at midnight of 14/15 August, 1947 provisionally?

stem: Mountbatten Plan (June 1947) provided for a referendum in which of the following province(s)?
expl: The important points of the Mountbatten Plan (3 June, 1947 AD) were – Punjab and Bengal Legislative Assemblies would meet in two groups, Hindus and Muslims, to vote for partition. If a simple majority of either group voted for partition, then these provinces would be partitioned. Sindh would take its own decision. Referendum in NWFP, Sindh, Baluchistan and Sylhet district of Assam would decide the fate of these areas. Since the congress had conceded a unifi ed India, all their other points would be met- (i) Independence for princely states ruled out, they would either join India or Pakistan. (ii) Independence for Bengal ruled out. (iii) Accession of Hyderabad to Pakistan ruled out (Mountbatten supported the congress on this).

stem: January 26,1950 was chosen for the enforcement of the Constitution because:

options.label: b
options.text: ‘Quit India Movement’ was begun on this date in 1942.

options.label: c
options.text: Congress had celebrated 26 January, 1930 as the fi rst Independence Day.

expl: In the year 1929 AD, at the annual session of Congress held at Lahore, ‘Purna Swaraj’ or Complete Independence was accepted as the goal of the Congress. On the banks of the river Ravi, at midnight on 31 December, 1929 AD, the tricolour fl ag of Indian Independence was unfurled amidst cheer and jubilation. 26 January, 1930 AD was marked as the fi rst Independence Day, which was to be so celebrated every year. To commemorate this historic day, it was decided to enforce the Constitution on 26 January, 1950 AD.
